policy_name: ARP Act Child Care Stabilization Grants

fields.name: total_stabilization_funding
fields.description: Total federal appropriation for child care stabilization grants under Section 2202 of the ARP Act.
fields.causal_relevance: Total funding available determines the scale of subgrants and set-aside activities that lead agencies can implement.

evidence.evidence_quote: Section 2202.  $23,975,000,000 for child care stabilization grants,  available until September 30, 2023.

fields.name: tribal_base_amount
fields.description: Base amount awarded to each individual tribal lead agency (not part of a consortium) for stabilization grants.
fields.causal_relevance: Base amount provides a minimum funding level for each tribal lead agency, affecting their ability to administer the program.

evidence.evidence_quote: The base amount for individual tribes (not  part of a consortium) is $30,000.

fields.name: state_minimum_subgrant_percentage
fields.description: Minimum percentage of stabilization funds that states and territories must spend as subgrants to qualified child care providers.
fields.causal_relevance: This requirement determines the minimum amount of funding that must flow directly to providers as subgrants.
kg_links: LeadAgency:State, Territory, and Tribal Lead Agencies

evidence.evidence_quote: Lead agencies must spend most stabilization funds (at least 90 percent for states  and territories and at least 80 percent for tribes) as subgrants to qualified child care providers to support the stability of the child care sector during and after the  COVID-19 public health emergency.

policy_parameters.name: tribal_minimum_subgrant_percentage
policy_parameters.description: Minimum percentage of stabilization funds that tribes must spend as subgrants to qualified child care providers.

evidence.evidence_quote: Lead agencies must spend most stabilization funds (at least 90 percent for states  and territories and at least 80 percent for tribes) as subgrants to qualified child care providers to support the stability of the child care sector during and after the  COVID-19 public health emergency.

policy_parameters.name: arp_act_enactment_date
policy_parameters.description: Date the American Rescue Plan Act was signed into law, used as a reference date for provider eligibility and non-supplantation baseline.

evidence.evidence_quote: Child Care Stabilization Grants Appropriated in the American Rescue Plan  (ARP) Act (Public Law 117-2) signed into law on March 11, 2021.

policy_parameters.name: obligation_deadline
policy_parameters.description: Deadline by which all stabilization funds must be obligated by states, territories, and tribes.

evidence.evidence_quote: September 30, 2022 – All stabilization funds must be obligated by states,  territories, and tribes.

policy_parameters.name: liquidation_deadline
policy_parameters.description: Deadline by which all stabilization funds must be liquidated by states, territories, and tribes.

evidence.evidence_quote: September 30, 2023 – All stabilization funds must be liquidated by  states, territories, and tribes.

policy_parameters.name: interim_obligation_milestone
policy_parameters.description: Date by which lead agencies are strongly encouraged to obligate at least 50% of subgrant funds.

evidence.evidence_quote: December 11, 2021 – A state, territory, or tribe must notify ACF if it is  unable to obligate 50 percent of the CCDF stabilization funds it received  under the ARP Act by December 11, 2021.

policy_parameters.name: tuition_relief_income_threshold
policy_parameters.description: Income threshold below which families should be prioritized for tuition and copayment relief.

evidence.evidence_quote: If a provider is unable to provide relief from copayments and tuition payments for all families enrolled in the program, they should prioritize doing so for families most in need of relief and target families earning below 85 percent of the State Median Income.

policy_parameters.name: provider_licensing_cutoff_date
policy_parameters.description: Date by which providers must have obtained licensing, regulation, or registration to qualify under one eligibility condition.

evidence.evidence_quote: A licensed, regulated, or registered child care provider in the state,  territory, or tribe that obtained such certification no later than March 11,  2021, and meets applicable state and local health and safety requirements  at the time of application for a subgrant.

policy_parameters.name: waiver_expiration_date
policy_parameters.description: Date by which temporary CCDBG waivers expire, after which providers must meet health and safety and background check requirements.

evidence.evidence_quote: We remind lead agencies that these temporary waivers expire on  September 30, 2021, after which lead agencies will need to support CCDF  providers in meeting health and safety and background checks.

policy_parameters.name: reimbursement_start_date
policy_parameters.description: Start date for expenses that can be reimbursed with stabilization funds for past costs.

evidence.evidence_quote: lead agencies are strongly encouraged to make subgrant funds  available to qualified child care providers to reimburse them for their costs  incurred after the declaration of the public health emergency on January 31,  2020, for any of the uses of funds outlined above, as long as those uses were  made in response to the COVID-19 public health emergency

policy_parameters.name: small_provider_employee_threshold
policy_parameters.description: Employee count threshold for defining small child care providers eligible for special application periods.

evidence.evidence_quote: For example, lead agencies can  limit applications in the first 2 weeks after the application is posted to  child care providers with fewer than 20 employees and those that have  501(c)(3) non-profit status.

policy_parameters.name: reallotment_minimum_amount
policy_parameters.description: Minimum amount of funds available for reallotment; below this amount, funds revert to the federal government.

evidence.evidence_quote: 45 C.F.R. 98.64(b)(2)(ii) says that funds will not be realloted (but will instead revert to the federal government) if  the amount available for reallotment is less than $25,000.

summary: Document-grounded initial state. Inputs: total_stabilization_funding=23975000000 USD; tribal_base_amount=30000 USD; state_minimum_subgrant_percentage=90 percent. Fixed policy parameters: tribal_minimum_subgrant_percentage=80 percent; arp_act_enactment_date=2021-03-11 date; obligation_deadline=2022-09-30 date; liquidation_deadline=2023-09-30 date; interim_obligation_milestone=2021-12-11 date; tuition_relief_income_threshold=85 percent of State Median Income; provider_licensing_cutoff_date=2021-03-11 date; waiver_expiration_date=2021-09-30 date; reimbursement_start_date=2020-01-31 date; small_provider_employee_threshold=20 employees; reallotment_minimum_amount=25000 USD.
